title: The Cold Hidden Ocean
question: How does heat move through the ocean from the surface to the deep?
hook: Tropical surface water can top 30 °C, yet most of the ocean's water stays at around 0-3 °C.
idea: Surface water cools as it leaves the tropics, sinks and returns at depth, so the vast deep ocean stays cold and uniform.

beats.prompt: A warm current leaves the tropics and slowly loses heat as it heads poleward. What happens to that water next?

choices.label: It stays on the surface and keeps flowing poleward forever
choices.feedback: Cooling makes the water denser, so it does not stay at the surface.

choices.label: It becomes denser, sinks and flows back toward the equator at depth
It warms up again because it is moving
choices.feedback: Moving water does not reheat itself; the current cools as it leaves the tropics.

choices.label: It freezes solid near the poles and stops
choices.feedback: The water sinks and keeps circulating as a deep current rather than stopping.

beats.explain: Cooling water grows denser and sinks, and changes in temperature and density carry it back toward the equator as a deep current.

beats.prompt: Put these steps of the ocean's slow overturning loop in order.
items: A warm surface current cools as it leaves the tropics
A deep current carries it back toward the equator
It wells back up toward the surface
beats.explain: Water cools and sinks, travels back toward the equator at depth, and eventually rises again.

beats.prompt: Match each part of the ocean to its typical temperature.
beats.explain: With the Sun nearly overhead the tropical surface can top 30 °C, water beside sea ice is about −2 °C, and deep water stays at a uniform 0-3 °C.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Calm wind and strong sunshine can warm a layer at the surface
Below that layer the temperature can drop sharply with depth
Experts call this daytime pattern a diurnal thermocline
So a reading needs no note of the depth it was taken at
beats.explain: Because temperature can vary so much with depth, especially by day, the depth of a measurement has to be stated.
